title: Monitor and protect ML and AI solutions
objective: Continuously observe and remediate model quality, data changes, system performance, costs, and access controls.

prerequisites.title: Safely deploy and automate ML and AI workflows

sections.title: Detecting Production Quality Degradation and Data Drift
paragraphs: Production monitoring requires more than tracking endpoint availability and latency. ML engineers compare the distribution of input data, the distribution of predictions, quality when ground-truth labels are available, and results by data segment against baselines established during training or approval.

SageMaker Model Monitor can monitor changes in data quality, model quality, bias, and feature attributes for production SageMaker models. However, monitoring results are not the causes themselves, so engineers investigate, together with lineage information, what changed in data ingestion, preprocessing, the model version, or user requirements.

sources.label: MLA-C02 Exam Guide: Operations, Monitoring, and Protection
Monitoring Data and Model Quality Using Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor

sections.title: Optimize performance, cost, and availability together
paragraphs: After reviewing inference latency and errors, operations personnel revisit the model, instances, autoscaling, input size, caching, and queuing. They do not determine capacity based solely on CPU utilization; instead, they compare request volume, queue length, latency, error rate, model processing time, and user impact over the same period.

Apply cost-reduction changes only after confirming that quality and service objectives are met. Even when reducing idle capacity, define the minimum capacity for sudden load, the time required to scale, failure handling, and budget alarms, then validate the results using post-change metrics.

sources.label: MLA-C02 Exam Guide: Operations, Monitoring, and Protection

sections.title: Protect data, models, and endpoints at every boundary
paragraphs: Security professionals do not treat training data, model artifacts, prompts, inference inputs and outputs, and logs as having the same exposure scope. They design encryption at rest and in transit, least-privilege IAM roles, network reachability, secrets management, and audit logs according to each data flow.

When investigating access to an inference endpoint, verify the calling principal, effective IAM permissions, endpoint policies, VPC paths, security groups, and access to logs. Broad administrative permissions and public settings may speed up development, but they increase the risks of data leakage and losing the ability to track changes.

sources.label: MLA-C02 Exam Guide: Operations, Monitoring, and Protection

checkpoints.prompt: In a production demand-forecasting model, the overall error rate has not changed, but the prediction error for a specific product has increased. Which investigation should the person responsible conduct first?

choices.text: Delete the logs for all models and wait for the next prediction.
choices.explanation: This would eliminate the evidence needed to investigate the cause.

choices.text: Increase only the number of instances without checking latency.
choices.explanation: There is no evidence that this addresses the cause of the quality degradation.

choices.text: Compare the target product’s input distribution, preprocessing, model version, ground-truth data, and group-level quality metrics with those from the baseline period.
choices.explanation: This helps isolate data changes or quality degradation that do not appear in the overall metrics.

checkpoints.prompt: The person responsible for reducing the cost of an inference endpoint wants to ensure that quality and availability are not compromised. Which approach is the most appropriate?

choices.text: Compare request volume, latency, error rate, processing time, minimum capacity, and scaling time, then validate the results after the change using the same metrics.
choices.explanation: This makes it possible to assess the impact on service objectives, not just the cost.

choices.text: Immediately reduce all capacity to zero without checking usage.
choices.explanation: This could prevent the endpoint from processing user requests.

choices.text: Look only at the budget and stop monitoring quality and error rates.
choices.explanation: This makes it impossible to detect the impact of cost reductions on users.

checkpoints.prompt: The person responsible for an inference API that handles sensitive data wants to prevent unnecessary access from outside while maintaining auditability. Which design is most appropriate?

choices.text: To accelerate development, expose the endpoint publicly and grant administrator permissions to all users.
choices.explanation: This would lead to unnecessary access to sensitive data and make changes impossible to trace.

choices.text: Use a least-privilege IAM role for each calling principal, and configure encryption, the required network reachability, secrets management, and audit logs for each data path.
choices.explanation: This aligns access controls and audit trails with the flow of the data.

choices.text: Call the API using only a shared access key, without retaining audit logs.
choices.explanation: This makes it impossible to identify the actors involved or investigate the incident afterward.
